title: Python: D4 staticmethod in BUILTIN_INSTANCE_CLASSES is callable since 3.10
description: Reported by the Opus review of #150 (not yet probed): class D(staticmethod, B) resolves B.__call__ although staticmethod.__call__ wins on the MRO, so N3 gives a false edge. Decide whether staticmethod (and classmethod) leave the exemption set or the MRO order is read; fixtures; mutation checks.
implementationNotes: Built (DEC-303 (a31) item 5, D4): BUILTIN_CLASS_DEFINED_NAMES (staticmethod -> __call__) in src/python/calls.ts; methodLookup returns external/external-base when an unshadowed builtin base earlier in the MRO defines the looked-up name, so it never reaches a later in-repo entry; builtinClassBaseName factored out of isBuiltinClassBase. classmethod keeps its place in BUILTIN_INSTANCE_CLASSES (it has no __call__); staticmethod stays in it for the constructor rule. N3 refuses the site (stays name / run-time-bound per (a31) Q1). Fixture: D(staticmethod, B) no edge, bin nameNotBound 1; positive twins D(classmethod|int|Exception, B) reach B.__call__; D(B, staticmethod) still edges; nested E(staticmethod), D(E, B) no edge. Mutation: emptying the table set goes red (1), source restored, green (218 pass). Also closed GCLI-97. NOT MEASURED: no corpus re-measure (not requested); other builtins' defined names are not tabulated, only staticmethod.__call__.
